title: Instant Infer — onramp messaging and pricing playbook
body:
Purpose:
This brief captures a fresh set of developer-first messaging hooks and pricing language to test with small-to-mid engineering teams during self-serve onboarding. Goal: increase 30-day active devs and reduce time-to-first-successful-inference call while preserving transparency around unit economics and predictable billing.

Audience:
- Primary: Individual engineers and small product teams evaluating an inference API for early integration (MVP to prod).
- Secondary: Platform and infra leads evaluating hosted options for predictable cost and SLA guarantees.

Core positioning (single sentence):
"Instant Infer" is a developer-first inference API that gets models answering in production-ready latency with minimal integration work and predictable per-token economics so dev teams can iterate quickly without cost surprises.

Key value props (developer-centric ordering):
1) Ship in minutes, iterate forever.
- 3 lines of code, immediate streaming responses, and sample prompts for common patterns (chat, summarization, classification).
- Pre-baked SDK snippets, a CLI to run local smoke tests, and a one-click playground to validate LLM outputs before committing.

2) Predictable unit economics, no surprises.
- Clear per-token pricing for generation + per-embedding unit. Transparent rounding rules and readout in the SDK.
- Cost controls built into the account (per-route caps, soft limits, dev quotas).

3) Production defaults that reduce ops overhead.
- Reasonable defaults for batching, caching, and KV reuse that avoid manual tuning for early workloads.
- Built-in fallbacks: cheaper quantized model variants and regional routing when capacity tight.

4) Developer-first observability.
- Token-level cost/latency traces, per-request sampling, and a replayable request log for debug.
- Quick links from the console to sample failing prompts and recommended mitigation.

Quickstart angles (copy-ready hooks for marketing and microcopy):
- 30s dev pitch: "Call the API, stream the first tokens, see answers in <1s — pay only for what you use."
- 5-min integration: "Install SDK, paste your API key, run example: chat.reply('summarize this ticket')."
- 1-commit-to-prod: "From first successful call to backing inference in production with rate limits and cost controls in a single day."

Suggested quickstart checklist (developer flow):
1. Create account, copy API key (UI shows cost estimate based on sample prompt).
2. Install SDK and run quickstart: `npm i @redwood/infer && node examples/hello.js`.
3. Hit the playground to tune prompt; copy the final request to your app.
4. Enable per-route soft caps and set environment-specific keys.
5. Monitor usage dashboard for first 24h; apply recommended batching if latency stable.

Pricing language — consumer-focused drafts (short variants for UI and billing emails):
- Variant A (simplicity-first): "Pay by the token: generation and embedding tokens billed per 1K. No minimums, no hidden rounding — see cost estimate in the SDK."
- Variant B (predictability-first): "Per-token pricing with optional Reserved Capacity for predictable spend and lower committed unit pricing. Start pay-as-you-go; upgrade when you need predictable throughput."
- Variant C (developer-control-first): "Set per-route budgets and default batching rules to keep dev experiments under control. We’ll notify you at 60%/80%/100% of route budget with one-click escalation."

Competitive positioning notes (quick bullets to test in sales snippets):
- Vs large cloud AI endpoints: emphasize the dev ergonomics (streaming + SDK examples), plus transparent token math and built-in cost controls versus opaque inference bundles.
- Vs simple LLM APIs: highlight production defaults (autoscaling policies, fallbacks to quantized variants) and observability that matters once the feature is live.
- Vs self-hosted runtimes: prometheus-grade telemetry and zero infra ops during the evaluation phase; call out easy path to Dedicated/Private when customers outgrow hosted.

Framing experiments and A/B test matrix (ideas for 4-week cycles):
- Experiment 1: Microcopy on pricing page — Variant A (per-token clarity) vs Variant B (reserved-first). Metric: conversion to first successful API call.
- Experiment 2: Quickstart CTA — "Start in 5 minutes" vs "Start and estimate cost". Metric: 7-day retention and average spend.
- Experiment 3: Onboarding email — include sample cost estimate vs not. Metric: 24h activation.

Sample microcopy and one-liners to use across landing, docs, and emails:
- "From first call to production-ready in a single afternoon."
- "Per-token clarity — know exactly what each inference costs."
- "Developer defaults that save ops time, not your time."
- "Measure latency and cost at the token level."

Risk and friction tokens (what to surface early):
- Explain rounding and how streaming affects billed tokens. Small sample snippet in the SDK README to show token counting.
- Clarify how cached responses (prefix/KV) are billed versus fresh generation.
- Call out reserved capacity pricing thresholds early for teams that plan >10M tokens/day.

Sales & enablement snippets (short bullets for SDRs/AE):
- "If you want to demo with a real prompt, we’ll spin a sandbox with 1M test tokens and a playbook for cost-control in 30 minutes."
- "Our SDK shows a live cost estimate for each example — helps set expectations in demos."

Operational hooks for product/engineering (how to make the messaging real quickly):
- Expose a client-side cost-estimator API that computes rough token cost for a given prompt + model selection.
- Add a quickstart mode in the console: preconfigure an API key with dev quotas and a button to run the sample script in Cloud Shell.
- Add an FAQ about billing and reserved capacity thresholds near the pricing panel.

Measurement plan (what success looks like):
- Activation: % of new sign-ups that make a successful inference call in 48 hours (target +15% after changes).
- Cost surprises: % of customers contacting billing with unexpected charges (target: reduce by 50%).
- Developer retention: 7-day active dev rate and 30-day active dev rate increases (benchmarks to be set vs control cohort).

Next steps and proposed timeline (6-week sprint):
- Week 1: Lock microcopy variants and implement client cost estimator (eng + SDK).
- Week 2: Update console quickstart flow and add prefilled dev quota.
- Week 3: Launch A/B tests on pricing page and onboarding email.
- Week 4-6: Collect data, iterate copy, and push best-performing variant to all traffic.

Open questions (should decide before launch):
- Exact thresholds and discounts for reserved capacity tiers — product to define by end of Week 1.
- What example prompts should be pre-bundled in the quickstart for best conversion across categories (chat, search, summarization)?
- How aggressive should the default per-route soft cap be for new dev accounts?

Appendix: sample SDK snippet (docs-friendly pseudo code for quickstart playground)

// Node quickstart
import Redwood from '@redwood/infer'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'rwd-small-v1', prompt: 'Summarize the following ticket in 2 lines: ...' })
console.log(res.text)

Notes: include a small inline cost estimate returned with the response object (e.g., { estimated_cost_usd: '0.00012' }) and show a link to the dashboard spend view.

——
Raw brainstorm fragments and microcopy variants (working notes):
- "Start in seconds, control in minutes."
- "Streaming first, surprises never."
- "We price per token — you choose when to commit to reserved throughput."
- "Developer defaults that get more accurate with production data."

Document owner/next review: Aisha Patel — sync with Product (Leah Cohen) and Applied ML (Marco Nguyen) before pushing to marketing.
